reason: Everything I open is phone photos, screenshots and PDFs, and Explorer plus whatever opens them already handles that. I would poke at it once or twice with a weird file, but nothing here fixes a problem I actually have.
why_switch_or_not: The long format list (AVIF, WebP, JXL, RAW, PSD) only matters to me if something I get actually fails, and so far it hasn't. The speed numbers are for people flicking through thousands of pictures, and I double-click one file at a time. Making it default means ticking formats myself in Windows Settings, and I would not bother for a viewer I don't need. The HEIC part needs the same Microsoft extension as Photos, so no gain there.
current_app_pros: Explorer thumbnails show me what I need, double-click just opens the picture in whatever Windows picks, and I never have to set anything up or think about it.
current_app_pains: Nothing really. Occasionally a WebP or AVIF from the web won't open or shows no thumbnail, and then I just convert it online or open it in the browser.
objection: It's an unknown .exe from one person, and the page doesn't say it's signed or open source. I'm not going to make something I don't know my default for opening files all day.
would_change_my_mind: Proof it's code-signed or open source with a reputable review, plus a file I actually need that Windows can't open and that it opens with one click.
